newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu adviser seeks Israel budget reform.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu adviser seeks Israel budget reform.

text.p: The chief economic adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Monday he would recommend reforming the process of preparing Israel's budget.
Economic adviser Moshe Leon said he would suggest the Treasury begin with a "zero budget" in 1998 rather than building on the previous year's budget.
Under the current practice of preparing the national budget, the previous year's budget is adjusted for inflation, one-time expenses are removed and new expenditures are added on.
Leon said building an entirely new budget based on the current government's priorities would save money. He cited health as one area that would benefit from more funding.
Leon said a special committee should be set up to determine the government's spending priorities.
